subject: GCP Marketplace private offer — batch redemption tactics and cadence
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@overturelabs.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Park <lydia.park@overturelabs.com>, gcp-marketplace@google.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer timeline — batch redemption idea

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We reviewed the draft private offer and want to propose a slightly different drawdown approach that aligns with our internal procurement windows. Instead of a steady monthly burn, we were hoping to: 

- Trigger three larger "redemption batches" across Q4 and Q1 (target dates attached)
- Use a single bulk invoice per redemption event (to simplify AP)
- Build a governance checkpoint before each batch (30-day notice + spike protection)

Attached is a proposed schedule (overtures_po_schedule.xlsx) and our PO template. Can Redwood confirm whether the GCP private offer can support batched SKUs or whether we need separate SKUs per tranche? Also calling out routing: we'd prefer consumption to come from the same private-offer SKU to avoid reconciliation complexity.

If you think it helps, include finance and marketplace PMs on the call. Samira

Attachment: overtures_po_schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@overturelabs.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Lydia Park <lydia.park@overturelabs.com>, gcp-marketplace@google.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer timeline — batch redemption idea

Samira — appreciate the clear schedule. Quick answers up front: Redwood can support both models, but the operational trade-offs differ. Short summary: 

- Single private-offer SKU with batched redemptions: simplest for your GL (single SKU) but requires us to set up a redemption webhook and reconciliation tag so we can attribute usage to each batch for invoicing.
- Distinct SKU per tranche: cleaner for GCP billing traceability and reduces manual reconciliation on our side, but creates more SKUs to manage on the marketplace.

Questions we have before we finalize: 
1) Do you need a single invoice per batch or one invoice aggregating multiple batches? (your note said single bulk invoice per redemption — confirming).
2) Who at Overture will sign the 30-day governance SLA? We'll need a named contact for the approval window to automate canary/fallback timing.

Marissa — can you pull the marketplace team runbook for batched redemptions and confirm whether we can rely on a single SKU + metadata tags to satisfy GCP reporting? If not, we should propose a lightweight SKU-per-tranche pattern.

Proposing a working call Wed 8/12 10am PT to align on finance and ops. Vivek

Signature: Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@overturelabs.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Lydia Park <lydia.park@overturelabs.com>, gcp-marketplace@google.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer timeline — batch redemption idea

Hi all — pulled the relevant notes from the marketplace playbook. High level: GCP supports both, but our preferred pattern for private-offer consumption that eases month-end reconciliations is: 

- Use one private-offer SKU for the contract, and encode a consumption metadata tag ("redemption_batch=2026Q4-A", etc.) on the redemption event.
- Redwood will emit a reconciliation CSV after each batch showing token counts and matching metadata so Overture AP can net against the PO.
- For invoicing: we can produce a single invoice per batch (as requested). For ACID-style traceability, we recommend a short-lived internal ledger entry per redemption that mirrors GCP's usage report.

Risks / work items:
- GCP billing exports are not guaranteed to include custom metadata fields to downstream exports — where necessary we add a small middleware reconciliation job in Redwood to join internal redemption events to raw billing lines.
- We need Overture to commit to the approval owner (30-day governance check) and confirm preferred invoice email.

I've attached the updated private-offer term PDF (gcp_private_offer_terms_v2.pdf) showing the batch/redemption clauses we would request. If that looks good, we can draft the DocuSign and schedule the first governance checkpoint for 2026-11-01.

Attachment: gcp_private_offer_terms_v2.pdf (pdf)

Marissa Cole
Director, Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@overturelabs.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@overturelabs.com>, jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>, gcp-marketplace@google.com
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer timeline — batch redemption idea

Thanks Marissa — this format should work for our AP team. Quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Approval owner will be me (Lydia Park, Finance Manager). I can review and approve governance checks; will put a delegated backup (Samira) in case I am out.
2) Invoice email: ap-overtures@overturelabs.com. Please route DocuSign and final invoice to that address.
3) On the metadata approach: we prefer the single SKU + metadata tag model to keep the marketplace listing tidy. We understand you'll add a reconciliation CSV after each batch.

We'll review the terms PDF and get back by EOD Friday if anything needs to be redlined. Lydia

Signature: Lydia Park
Finance Manager, Overture Labs

From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@overturelabs.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@overturelabs.com>, gcp-marketplace@google.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer timeline — batch redemption idea

Following up after Lydia's note and our internal scoping. Operational steps we will take once PO is signed: 

1) Implement a short-lived redemption token flow on Redwood that attaches a redemption_batch tag to each consumption event.
2) Emit a reconciliation CSV within 48 hours of a batch trigger to ap-overtures@overturelabs.com with usage rows and invoiceable tokens.
3) Add a canary policy: for each batch there will be an initial 72-hour canary window capped at 15% of the tranche. If no anomalies, full tranche opens. This protects Overture from sudden over-consumption and preserves SLA.

Action items: 
- Overture: confirm ap email (Lydia confirmed ap-overtures@overturelabs.com) and governance owner (Lydia).
- Redwood: produce final PDF with the canary clause (we will append to the terms and re-upload to DocuSign).
- Schedule: first batch trigger target 2026-11-01 pending DocuSign completion.

I'll attach the suggested canary clause text in the DocuSign envelope. If Overture wants, we can run a short pre-batch smoke test on a staging SKU the week before.

Jonas Weber
Senior Product Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachment: (see DocuSign link)
